title: Weather and seasons
goal: By the end of this lesson you can describe the weather and temperature, talk about the four seasons, and survive a Quebec winter conversation about frette, slush and poudrerie.

body: Most weather descriptions use *il fait* + adjective: *Il fait beau.* (It's nice.) *Il fait chaud.* (It's hot.) *Il fait froid.* (It's cold.) The *il* is impersonal, like 'it' in English.
Temperatures also use *il fait*: *Il fait vingt degrés.* *Il fait moins quinze.* (It's minus fifteen.)

head: French
English
rows: It's sunny. (common in Quebec; also Il y a du soleil.)

learn.tip: Il fait + adjective. Never 'il est froid' for the weather: that means 'he is cold (to the touch)'.

learn.h: Weather verbs and il y a
body: Some weather has its own verb, used only with *il*: *Il pleut.* (It's raining, from *pleuvoir*.) *Il neige.* (It's snowing.) *Il vente.* (It's windy.) *Il grêle.* (It's hailing.)
Others use *il y a* + partitive: *Il y a du vent.* *Il y a du soleil.* *Il y a des nuages.* *Il y a du brouillard.* (fog)
For the future: *Il va pleuvoir.* *Il va faire beau.* *Il va neiger demain.*

head: Verb / phrase
English
rows: Il vente. / Il y a du vent.

body: All four seasons are masculine: *le printemps, l'été, l'automne, l'hiver*.
To say 'in' a season: *au printemps*, but *en été*, *en automne*, *en hiver* (the three that start with a vowel).

head: Season
'In …'
Example
rows: En été, il fait chaud et humide.

learn.tip: Only printemps takes au: it's the only season starting with a consonant.

body: *Il fait frette* is the informal Quebec way to say *il fait très froid*: it's freezing. Use it with friends, not in an essay.

*La slush* (also spelled *sloche*) is the slushy brown snow in the streets. *La poudrerie* is snow blown by the wind; it's a neutral Quebec word you'll hear on weather reports. Also: *il mouille* (informal: it's raining), *une tempête de neige*, and *le facteur vent* (windchill).

examples.en: It's been raining for two days.
It snows a lot in January.

Il y a des nuages, mais il fait chaud.

examples.fr: En automne, les feuilles sont rouges et jaunes.

examples.fr: Il ne fait pas froid, il fait doux.

examples.en: Put on your toque, it's freezing!

examples.fr: Il y a de la slush partout.
Attention, il y a de la poudrerie sur l'autoroute.
examples.en: Careful, there's blowing snow on the highway.

quebec.intro: Winter is the national topic of conversation in Quebec, and it has its own vocabulary: frette for very cold, slush for dirty melting snow, and poudrerie for snow whipped up by the wind.

items.note: informal; frette is stronger than froid

items.qc: de la slush / de la sloche

items.std: de la neige soulevée par le vent
items.note: neutral Quebec term, used on the news

items.qc: le facteur vent / le refroidissement éolien
items.note: both heard on Quebec weather reports

items.note: en malade = really, extremely; very informal

luh-prin-TAHN; p and s are silent at the end.

dialogue.fr: Le matin, il va faire moins vingt-cinq avec le facteur vent.
dialogue.en: In the morning, it's going to be minus twenty-five with the windchill.

dialogue.fr: Et l'après-midi, il va neiger. Il va y avoir de la poudrerie sur la 20.
dialogue.en: And in the afternoon, it's going to snow. There's going to be blowing snow on Highway 20.

dialogue.fr: Bon, je prends l'autobus. Et dimanche?
dialogue.en: OK, I'm taking the bus. And Sunday?

dialogue.fr: Dimanche, il va faire doux, plus deux. Mais avec la slush partout...
dialogue.en: On Sunday, it's going to be mild, plus two. But with slush everywhere...

speak.model: Aujourd'hui, il fait froid. Il fait moins douze et il y a du vent. Il ne neige pas.

speak.prompt: Describe each season where you live in one sentence.
speak.model: Au printemps, il pleut. En été, il fait chaud et humide. En automne, il fait frais. En hiver, il neige beaucoup.

speak.prompt: Complain about the winter like a Quebecer, using frette and slush.
speak.model: Il fait frette à matin, pis y a de la slush partout!

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your favourite and least favourite season and the weather in each.
write.model: Ma saison préférée, c'est l'été. En été, il fait chaud et il y a du soleil. On va au parc et à la plage. Je n'aime pas le mois de mars. Il fait gris, il y a de la slush et il vente beaucoup. Mais au moins, le printemps arrive bientôt!

quiz.why: Au printemps; en été / automne / hiver.

quiz.q: Which is a weather verb used only with 'il'?
quiz.why: Pleuvoir only exists as il pleut, il va pleuvoir, etc.
le printemps, l'été, l'automne, l'hiver: all masculine.
